defaults.permitted_development: House extensions can be permitted development in Wales where they stay within Class A limits on projection, height, eaves, width and highway relationships. Front extensions and prominent side work are much more restricted.

rules.height_rules: Single-storey rear and side extensions should not exceed 4m in height. Eaves should not be higher than the eaves of the existing part of the house they project from, and no extension should exceed the existing roof height.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor. More-than-one-storey side extensions need a 1m setback from the principal elevation.
rules.boundary_rules: Where any part is within 2m of a boundary, eaves should not exceed 3m and overall height there should not exceed 4m. More-than-one-storey side extensions must be at least 10.5m from the opposite side boundary; more-than-one-storey rear upper floors must be at least 10.5m from the rear boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Extensions should not project beyond the principal elevation. Side extensions should not be nearer a highway than the existing side wall, or 5m from the highway, whichever is nearer. Verandas, raised platforms and roof terraces are not included in these rights.
rules.materials_rules: External wall and roof materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls in Wales narrow these rights. Side extensions on designated land are more restricted, two-storey side extensions are not permitted there, and Article 4 directions can remove further rights.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually needed for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be required.

rules.permitted_development: In Wales a house extension may stay within permitted development, but only where it satisfies the relevant Class A rules on projection, height, width and relationship to highways and the principal elevation.

rules.height_rules: Welsh house-extension height control is usually straightforward: single-storey rear and side work stays within 4m, the eaves should not rise above the part of the house extended, and no addition should exceed the existing roof height.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor. More-than-one-storey side extensions need a 1m setback from the principal elevation.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary rules in Wales are split by type of extension. Near-boundary parts keep to the 3m eaves and 4m height tests, while upper floors to side or rear extensions must clear the relevant 10.5m boundary distance.
rules.roof_rules: Extensions should not project beyond the principal elevation. Side extensions should not be nearer a highway than the existing side wall, or 5m from the highway, whichever is nearer. Verandas, raised platforms and roof terraces are not included in these rights.
rules.materials_rules: Match new wall and roof finishes closely to the existing house so the extension reads as part of the dwelling rather than an obvious add-on.

rules.boundary_rules: Where any part is within 2m of a boundary, eaves should not exceed 3m and overall height there should not exceed 4m. More-than-one-storey side extensions must be at least 10.5m from the opposite side boundary; more-than-one-storey rear upper floors must be at least 10.5m from the rear boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Extensions should not project beyond the principal elevation. Side extensions should not be nearer a highway than the existing side wall, or 5m from the highway, whichever is nearer. Verandas, raised platforms and roof terraces are not included in these rights.
rules.materials_rules: External wall and roof materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls in Wales narrow these rights. Side extensions on designated land are more restricted, two-storey side extensions are not permitted there, and Article 4 directions can remove further rights.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually needed for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be required.
